title: Shufro Rose & Co. LLC Has $12.28 Million Stake in Apple Inc. (AAPL)
text:
Shufro Rose & Co. LLC lessened its stake in shares of Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 3.4% in the 1st quarter, according to its most recent Form 13F filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The fund owned 73,200 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after selling 2,546 shares during the quarter. Apple comprises approximately 1.2% of Shufro Rose & Co. LLC’s portfolio, making the stock its 26th biggest position. Shufro Rose & Co. LLC’s holdings in Apple were worth $12,281,000 at the end of the most recent reporting period.
Other institutional investors also recently added to or reduced their stakes in the company. Condor Capital Management raised its position in Apple by 2.0% in the first quarter. Condor Capital Management now owns 50,238 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $8,429,000 after acquiring an additional 969 shares in the last quarter. Wade G W & Inc. raised its position in Apple by 1.8% in the first quarter. Wade G W & Inc. now owns 201,870 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $33,870,000 after acquiring an additional 3,664 shares in the last quarter. Blume Capital Management Inc. raised its position in Apple by 2.2% in the first quarter. Blume Capital Management Inc. now owns 75,445 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $12,658,000 after acquiring an additional 1,590 shares in the last quarter. Busey Trust CO purchased a new position in Apple in the first quarter worth $38,150,000. Finally, Motley Fool Asset Management LLC raised its position in Apple by 109.9% in the first quarter. Motley Fool Asset Management LLC now owns 94,452 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $15,847,000 after acquiring an additional 49,452 shares in the last quarter. Institutional investors and hedge funds own 58.07% of the company’s stock. Get Apple alerts:
Shares of NASDAQ:AAPL opened at $191.88 on Friday. The company has a current ratio of 1.46, a quick ratio of 1.37 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.80. Apple Inc. has a 12-month low of $147.30 and a 12-month high of $194.20. The stock has a market capitalization of $966.09 billion, a price-to-earnings ratio of 18.38, a price-to-earnings-growth ratio of 1.54 and a beta of 1.24.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last issued its quarterly earnings results on Tuesday, May 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.73 earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter, topping analysts’ consensus estimates of $2.69 by $0.04. Apple had a return on equity of 39.97% and a net margin of 21.55%. The firm had revenue of $61.14 billion for the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $60.94 billion. During the same period last year, the company earned $2.10 EPS. The firm’s quarterly revenue was up 15.6% on a year-over-year basis. sell-side analysts expect that Apple Inc. will post 11.42 earnings per share for the current year.
Apple announced that its Board of Directors has initiated a share repurchase program on Tuesday, May 1st that allows the company to repurchase $100.00 billion in outstanding shares. This repurchase authorization allows the iPhone maker to purchase up to 11.9% of its shares through open market purchases. Shares repurchase programs are often an indication that the company’s management believes its shares are undervalued.
In other Apple news, insider Angela J. Ahrendts sold 38,228 shares of the firm’s stock in a transaction dated Friday, May 4th. The stock was sold at an average price of $176.54, for a total value of $6,748,771.12. Following the sale, the insider now directly owns 90,967 shares of the company’s stock, valued at approximately $16,059,314.18. The sale was disclosed in a filing with the SEC, which can be accessed through this link . Also, COO Jeffrey E. Williams sold 15,652 shares of the firm’s stock in a transaction dated Monday, July 9th. The stock was sold at an average price of $190.18, for a total value of $2,976,697.36. Following the completion of the sale, the chief operating officer now directly owns 125,258 shares in the company, valued at $23,821,566.44. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . Over the last three months, insiders sold 168,738 shares of company stock worth $31,247,951. 0.08% of the stock is owned by corporate insiders.
Several research analysts have issued reports on AAPL shares. BidaskClub cut Apple from a “buy” rating to a “hold” rating in a research report on Friday, June 8th. Morgan Stanley cut their price objective on Apple from $203.00 to $200.00 and set an “overweight” rating for the company in a research report on Friday, April 20th. Bank of America reiterated a “buy” rating and issued a $220.00 price objective on shares of Apple in a research report on Friday, March 23rd. Rosenblatt Securities set a $180.00 price objective on Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research report on Wednesday, March 28th. Finally, Goldman Sachs Group set a $159.00 price objective on Apple and gave the stock a “neutral” rating in a research report on Tuesday, April 3rd. One analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, fifteen have issued a hold rating, thirty-two have given a buy rating and two have issued a strong buy rating to the company’s stock. The stock has a consensus rating of “Buy” and a consensus price target of $208.11.
Apple Profile
Apple Inc designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, and personal computers to consumers, and small and mid-sized businesses; and education, enterprise, and government customers worldwide. The company also sells related software, services, accessories, networking solutions, and third-party digital content and applications.
